summary: Bare 'per year'/'annual' wording cannot safely be normalized to benefit_year; governing plan definitions must control period semantics.
Reasonable-and-customary language is generally a dynamic adjudication policy; current parser logic can falsely infer a numeric R&C cap from unrelated dollar amounts in the same block.
Real insurer benefit rules commonly layer per-visit, annual, shared, visit-count, frequency, incident and lifetime limits, so a single maximum_amount plus period_kind is insufficient.
Direct-billing capability must be separated from member-plan claim eligibility and claim-payment certainty.
Coordination of benefits, eligibility conditions and predetermination need first-class modeling before pilot use.
recommended_next_action: Reviewer/Primary should reconcile the proposed schema/parser hardening before real plan documents are used for user-facing reimbursement estimates. Add fixtures T1-T8 from the artifact and preserve fail-closed behavior for unresolved semantics.
